title.zh: 卷一百〇五 列傳第三十五: 能吏
title.raw: 卷一百〇五 列傳第三十五: 能吏 Volume 105 Biographies 35: Capable Officials

sentences.zh: 能吏 ○大公鼎蕭文馬人望耶律鐸魯斡楊遵勖王棠

translations.literal: Capable Officials ○ Da Gongding, Xiao Wen, Ma Renwang, Yelü Duo, Luwo, Yang Zunxu, Wang Tang
translations.idiomatic: Capable Officials — Da Gongding, Xiao Wen, Ma Renwang, Yelü Duo, Luwo, Yang Zunxu, and Wang Tang

sentences.zh: 漢以璽書賜二千石，唐疏刺史、縣令於屏，以示獎率，故二史有《循吏》、《良吏》之傳。

translations.literal: The Han used imperial-sealed documents to bestow on the two-thousand-dan officials; the Tang inscribed prefects and county magistrates on screens to display encouragement and standards—hence the two histories have biographies of "Diligent Officials" and "Good Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, imperial edicts sealed with the dynastic seal were conferred on the two-thousand-dan officials; under the Tang, the names of prefects and county magistrates were inscribed on screens as models of reward and emulation—hence both histories include biographies of Diligent Officials and Good Officials.

sentences.zh: 遼自太祖創業，太宗撫有燕、薊，任賢使能之道，亦略備矣。

translations.literal: From the Liao, since Emperor Taizu founded the enterprise and Emperor Taizong pacified and held Yan and Ji, the way of appointing worthies and employing the able was also largely complete.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Emperor Taizu founded the Liao state and Emperor Taizong brought Yan and Ji under rule, the practice of appointing worthies and putting talent to use was largely in place as well.

sentences.zh: 然惟朝廷參置國官，吏州縣者多遵唐制。

translations.literal: Yet only at court were national offices jointly established; those who administered prefectures and counties mostly followed Tang institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet only at court were national offices established in concert; administration of prefectures and counties largely followed Tang practice.

sentences.zh: 歷世既久，選舉益嚴。

translations.literal: As generations passed, selection and appointment grew stricter.
translations.idiomatic: As generations passed, recruitment and selection grew ever stricter.

sentences.zh: 時又分遣重臣巡行境內，察賢否而進退之。

translations.literal: At the time they also dispatched senior ministers in separate missions to tour within the borders, examining worthiness and unworthiness to promote or dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent senior ministers on circuit through the realm to inspect officials and advance or remove them according to merit.

sentences.zh: 是以治民、理財、決獄、弭盜，各有其人。

translations.literal: Therefore in governing the people, managing finances, deciding cases, and quelling banditry, each had its man.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for governing the people, managing revenue, adjudicating cases, and suppressing banditry, there were men fit for each task.

sentences.zh: 考其德政，雖未足以與諸循、良之列，抑亦可謂能吏矣。

translations.literal: Examining their virtuous administration, although not sufficient to rank with the various diligent and good officials, they may still be called capable officials.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by their conduct in office, they may not fully measure up to the ranks of diligent and good officials, yet they may still be called capable administrators.

sentences.zh: 作《能吏傳》。

translations.literal: This composes the "Biographies of Capable Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Capable Officials."

sentences.zh: 大公鼎，渤海人，先世籍遼陽率賓縣。

translations.literal: Da Gongding was a man of Bohai; his forebears were registered in Shuai-bin County, Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Da Gongding was a Bohai native whose family had long been registered in Shuai-bin County in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 統和間，徙遼東豪右以實中京，因家於大定。

translations.literal: During the Tonghe era, powerful families of eastern Liao were moved to populate the Central Capital, and his family therefore settled in Dading.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe reign, powerful families of eastern Liao were relocated to populate the Central Capital, and his household thereafter made its home in Dading.

sentences.zh: 曾祖忠，禮賓使。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhong was Director of Ceremonial Reception.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhong served as Director of Ceremonial Reception.

sentences.zh: 父信，興中主簿。

translations.literal: His father Xin was Registrar of Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin was Registrar of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 公鼎幼莊願，長而好學。

translations.literal: Gongding in youth was solemn and earnest; grown, he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gongding was grave and dutiful as a boy and devoted himself to study as he grew.

sentences.zh: 咸雍十年，登進士第，調沈州觀察判官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianyong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Acting Investigating Commissioner of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Xianyong era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed acting investigating commissioner of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時遼東雨水傷稼，北樞密院大發瀕河丁壯以完堤防。

translations.literal: At the time rains in eastern Liao damaged the crops; the Northern Privy Council greatly mobilized able-bodied men along the river to complete the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time heavy rains in eastern Liao had damaged the harvest, and the Northern Privy Council conscripted large numbers of men along the riverbanks to repair the dikes.

sentences.zh: 有司承令峻急，公鼎獨曰：「邊障甫寧，大興役事，非利國便農之道。」

translations.literal: The offices, carrying out orders harshly and urgently, Gongding alone said: "The frontier has only just been pacified; to launch great labor projects is not the way to benefit the state and ease farming."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices enforced the order with harsh urgency, but Gongding alone said, "The frontier has only just settled down. To launch major corvée projects now is not the way to serve the state or ease the burden on farmers."

sentences.zh: 乃疏奏其事。

translations.literal: He then memorialized the matter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon submitted a memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之，罷役，水亦不為災。

translations.literal: The court assented, halted the labor, and the waters likewise did not become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his request, halted the corvée, and the floods never became a catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 瀕河千里，人莫不悅。

translations.literal: Along the river for a thousand li, none among the people failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand li along the river, the people were universally grateful.

sentences.zh: 改良鄉令，省徭役，務農桑，建孔子廟學，部民服化。

translations.literal: He reformed the magistrates of Liang Township, reduced corvée and labor service, devoted effort to farming and sericulture, built a Confucian temple and school, and the people of his district submitted to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Liang Township he streamlined local administration, reduced corvée, promoted farming and sericulture, and founded a Confucian temple and school; the people of his district were thoroughly won over.

sentences.zh: 累遷興國軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in due course to vice military commissioner of Xingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 時有隸鷹坊者，以羅畢為名，擾害田里。

translations.literal: At the time there were men attached to the Falcon Office who, under the name of "netting and closing," harassed and harmed the fields and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: At the time men attached to the imperial Falcon Office, operating under the name of "netting and closing" (for hawking), preyed on the countryside and harassed the farming districts.

sentences.zh: 歲久，民不堪。

translations.literal: Year after year, the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the people could endure it no longer.

sentences.zh: 公鼎言於上，即命禁戢。

translations.literal: Gongding spoke to the throne, and an order was immediately issued to forbid and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongding reported the abuse to the throne, and an immediate order was issued to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 會公鼎造朝，大臣諭上嘉納之意，公鼎曰：「一郡獲安，誠為大幸；

translations.literal: When Gongding came to court, a senior minister conveyed the emperor's intent to commend and accept his service; Gongding said: "That one commandery has found peace is truly a great fortune;
translations.idiomatic: When Gongding came to court, a senior minister conveyed the emperor's praise and approval. Gongding said, "That one commandery has found peace is indeed a great blessing;

sentences.zh: 他郡如此者眾，願均其賜於天下。」

translations.literal: many other commanderies suffer likewise—I wish to extend this grace equally to all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: yet many other commanderies suffer the same abuse. I beg that this benefit be extended equally throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 徙長春州錢帛都提點。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Chief Intendant of Cash and Silks at Changchunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as chief intendant of cash and silks at Changchunzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕如春水，貴主例為假貸，公鼎曰：「豈可輟官用，徇人情？」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to the spring hunt, noble ladies customarily sought loans; Gongding said: "How can one halt official funds to indulge personal favor?"
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went to the spring hunt, noble ladies routinely sought loans from the treasury. Gongding said, "How can official funds be suspended to indulge private favor?"

sentences.zh: 拒之。

translations.literal: He refused them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused them.

sentences.zh: 頗聞怨詈語，曰：「此吾職，不敢廢也。」

translations.literal: He heard much resentful cursing and said: "This is my duty—I dare not neglect it."
translations.idiomatic: He heard much bitter complaint, but said, "This is my duty, and I dare not neglect it."

sentences.zh: 俄拜大理卿，多所平反。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Director of the Court of Review and reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed director of the Court of Review and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 天祚即位，歷長寧軍節度使、南京副留守，改東京戶部使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Tianzuo took the throne, he served successively as Military Commissioner of Changning Army and Vice Guardian of the Southern Capital, then was changed to Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tianzuo acceded, he served successively as military commissioner of Changning Army and vice guardian of the Southern Capital, then was appointed commissioner of the Eastern Capital Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時盜殺留守蕭保先，始利其財，因而倡亂。

translations.literal: At the time bandits killed the Guardian Xiao Baoxian, at first coveting his wealth and thereby inciting disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits murdered the guardian Xiao Baoxian, at first for his wealth and thereby inciting wider disorder.

sentences.zh: 民亦互生猜忌，家自為鬥。

translations.literal: The people also mutually bred suspicion, and households fought among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The populace grew mutually suspicious, and households took up arms against one another.

sentences.zh: 公鼎單騎行郡，陳以禍福，眾皆投兵而拜曰：「是不欺我，敢弗聽命。」

translations.literal: Gongding rode alone through the commandery, setting forth fortune and misfortune; the multitude all cast down weapons and bowed, saying: "This man does not deceive us—we dare not disobey his command."
translations.idiomatic: Gongding rode alone through the commandery, explaining the consequences of obedience and rebellion. The people cast down their weapons and bowed, saying, "This man does not deceive us—we dare not disobey his command."

sentences.zh: 安輯如故。

translations.literal: Tranquility and order were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquility was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 拜中京留守，賜貞亮功臣，乘傳赴官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Guardian of the Central Capital, granted the title Meritorious Minister of Upright Integrity, and went to his post by relay.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed guardian of the Central Capital, granted the title Meritorious Minister of Upright Integrity, and traveled to his post by imperial relay.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊充斥，有遇公鼎於路者，即叩馬乞自新。

translations.literal: At the time bandits and robbers filled the land; those who met Gongding on the road would immediately knock on his horse and beg to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits and robbers filled the land. Those who met Gongding on the road would halt his horse and beg to reform.

sentences.zh: 公鼎給以符約，俾還業，聞者接踵而至。

translations.literal: Gongding gave them tally-pledges and enabled them to return to their occupations; those who heard came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Gongding issued them written pledges of amnesty and sent them back to their trades; word spread and others came in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，境內清肅。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days, the territory within the borders was clear and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the entire jurisdiction was pacified.

sentences.zh: 天祚聞之，加賜保節功臣。

translations.literal: Tianzuo heard of it and additionally granted him the title Meritorious Minister Who Guards Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianzuo heard of this, he additionally granted him the title Meritorious Minister Who Guards Integrity.

sentences.zh: 時人心反側，公鼎慮生變，請布恩惠以安之，為之肆赦。

translations.literal: At the time hearts were unsettled; Gongding feared trouble would arise, requested that favor be spread to settle them, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Popular sentiment was still unsettled. Fearing further unrest, Gongding petitioned for a display of imperial grace to reassure the people, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 公鼎累表乞歸，不許。

translations.literal: Gongding repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gongding repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 會奴賊張撒八率無賴嘯聚，公鼎欲擊而勢有不能。

translations.literal: When the slave-bandit Zhang Sabba led ruffians in clamorous assembly, Gongding wished to strike but found his strength insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: When the slave-rebel Zhang Sabba rallied desperadoes in open revolt, Gongding wished to attack but found his forces inadequate.

sentences.zh: 嘆曰：「吾欲謝事久矣，為世故所牽，不幸至此，豈命也夫！」

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "I have long wished to withdraw from office, yet was dragged along by worldly affairs; unhappily it has come to this—is it fate!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "I have long wished to leave office, yet worldly affairs kept me bound. To come to this unhappy pass—can it be fate?"

sentences.zh: 因憂憤成疾。

translations.literal: He thereby fell ill from worry and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill from worry and indignation.

sentences.zh: 保大元年卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoda he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Baoda era, at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 子昌齡，左承制；

translations.literal: His son Changling was Left Assistant Director;
translations.idiomatic: His son Changling served as left assistant director;

sentences.zh: 昌嗣，洺州刺史；

translations.literal: Changsi was Prefect of Mingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Changsi was prefect of Mingzhou;

sentences.zh: 昌朝，鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: Changchao was Military Commissioner of Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: and Changchao was military commissioner of Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 蕭文，字國華，外戚之賢者也。

translations.literal: Xiao Wen, styled Guohua, was a worthy man among the imperial affines.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Wen, styled Guohua, was a worthy man among the imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 父直善，安州防禦使。

translations.literal: His father Zhishan was Defense Commissioner of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhishan was defense commissioner of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 文篤誌力學，喜慍不形。

translations.literal: Wen was devoted in will and labored at learning; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was devoted in purpose and diligent in study; neither joy nor anger showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 大康初，掌秦越國王中丞司事，以才幹稱。

translations.literal: Early in Dakang he managed affairs of the Central Chancellor's Office of the King of Qinyue, and was famed for talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dakang era he managed affairs of the Central Chancellor's Office of the King of Qinyue and won renown for his ability.

sentences.zh: 尋知北面貼黃。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made Supervisor of Northern Draft Endorsements.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was appointed supervisor of northern draft endorsements.

sentences.zh: 王邦彥子爭蔭，數歲不能定，有司以聞。

translations.literal: The sons of Wang Bangyan disputed hereditary privilege; for several years it could not be settled, and the offices reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Wang Bangyan disputed hereditary privilege; for several years the case could not be settled, and the responsible offices reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命文詰之，立決。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wen to examine it, and he decided it at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wen to investigate, and he rendered an immediate decision.

sentences.zh: 車駕將還宮，承詔閱習儀衛，雖執事林林，指顧如一。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to return to the palace, he received an edict to review and drill the ceremonial guard; though the officers were numerous as a forest, his direction and glance were as one.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage was about to return to the palace, he received an edict to review and drill the ceremonial guard. Though the officers were numerous as trees in a forest, his commands were unified and precise.

sentences.zh: 遷同知奉國軍節度使，歷國舅都監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Associate Military Commissioner of Fengguo Army and served as Director of the Imperial Affines.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate military commissioner of Fengguo Army and later served as director of the imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 壽隆末，知易州，兼西南面安撫使。

translations.literal: Late in Shoulong he was made Administrator of Yizhou and concurrently Pacification Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Shoulong era he was appointed administrator of Yizhou and concurrently pacification commissioner of the southwestern circuit.

sentences.zh: 高陽土沃民富，吏其邑者，每黷於貨，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Gaoyang's soil was fertile and its people wealthy; those who governed its districts were repeatedly corrupt in goods, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyang had fertile soil and a wealthy populace, yet the officials who governed it were habitually corrupt, and the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 文始至，悉去舊弊，務農桑，崇禮教，民皆化之。

translations.literal: When Wen first arrived, he entirely removed old abuses, devoted effort to farming and sericulture, honored ritual teaching, and the people all were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen first arrived, he swept away old abuses, promoted farming and sericulture, and honored ritual instruction; the people were thoroughly transformed.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，百姓憂甚，文禱之輒雨。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought; the common people were deeply worried, and when Wen prayed, rain would come at once.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought afflicted the region and the people were deeply anxious; whenever Wen prayed, rain followed at once.

sentences.zh: 屬縣又蝗，議捕除之，文曰：「蝗，天災，捕之何益！」

translations.literal: A subordinate county again had locusts; they discussed catching and eliminating them. Wen said: "Locusts are a heaven-sent calamity—what use is catching them!"
translations.idiomatic: Locusts then appeared in a subordinate county, and officials proposed catching and destroying them. Wen said, "Locusts are a heaven-sent calamity—what use is catching them?"

sentences.zh: 但反躬自責，蝗盡飛去，遺者亦不食苗，散在草莽，為烏鵲所食。

translations.literal: He only turned inward and blamed himself; the locusts all flew away, and those left behind likewise did not eat the seedlings, scattering in the grass and thickets to be eaten by crows and magpies.
translations.idiomatic: He examined his own conduct instead. The locusts all flew away; those that remained did not eat the seedlings but scattered in the grass and thickets, where crows and magpies devoured them.

sentences.zh: 會霪雨不止，文復隨禱而霽。

translations.literal: When incessant heavy rain would not stop, Wen again prayed and it cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When incessant heavy rains followed, Wen prayed again and the skies cleared.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大熟。

translations.literal: That year there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a bountiful harvest.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以文可大用，遷唐古部節度使，高陽勒石頌之。

translations.literal: The court judged that Wen could be greatly employed, transferred him to Military Commissioner of the Tangut Circuit, and Gaoyang carved stone to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Wen fit for greater responsibility and transferred him to military commissioner of the Tangut circuit; Gaoyang carved a stone inscription in his praise.

sentences.zh: 後不知所終。

translations.literal: Later his end is not known.
translations.idiomatic: His later fate is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 馬人望，字儼叔，高祖胤卿，為石晉青州刺史，太宗兵至，堅守不降。

translations.literal: Ma Renwang, styled Yanshu, was a descendant of the High Ancestor Yin Qing, who served as Prefect of Qingzhou under the Later Jin of the Shi clan; when Emperor Taizong's army arrived, he held firm and would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Renwang, styled Yanshu, was descended from the High Ancestor Yin Qing, who had served as prefect of Qingzhou under the Later Jin. When Emperor Taizong's army arrived, Yin Qing held the city and refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 城破被執，太宗義而釋之，徙其族於醫巫閭山，因家焉。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was seized; Taizong, judging it righteous, released him and moved his clan to Mount Yiwulu, where they made their home.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was captured. Taizong, moved by his loyalty, released him and relocated his clan to Mount Yiwulu, where the family thereafter settled.

sentences.zh: 曾祖廷煦，南京留守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tingxu was Guardian of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tingxu was guardian of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 祖淵，中京副留守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuan was Vice Guardian of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuan was vice guardian of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 父詮，中京文思使。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Commissioner of Literary Thought at the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan was commissioner of literary thought at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 人望穎悟。

translations.literal: Renwang was keen and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang was exceptionally quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，長以才學稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, grown he was famed for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he won renown in adulthood for talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 咸雍中，第進士，為松山縣令。

translations.literal: During Xianyong he placed in the jinshi examination and became Magistrate of Songshan County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianyong era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Songshan County.

sentences.zh: 歲運澤州官炭，獨役松山，人望請於中京留守蕭吐渾均役他邑。

translations.literal: Each year official charcoal of Zezhou was transported, with corvée levied on Songshan alone; Renwang petitioned the Central Capital Guardian Xiao Tuhun to distribute the labor equally among other districts.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the transport of official charcoal from Zezhou imposed corvée on Songshan alone. Renwang petitioned the Central Capital guardian Xiao Tuhun to distribute the burden equally among neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 吐渾怒，下吏，系幾百日。

translations.literal: Tuhun was angry, had him sent down to the magistrate, and imprisoned him for nearly a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhun was enraged, had him arrested, and kept him imprisoned for nearly a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 復引詰之，人望不屈，蕭喜曰：「君為民如此，後必大用。」

translations.literal: He again summoned and interrogated him; Renwang did not yield. Xiao said with pleasure: "You act for the people thus—later you will surely be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: When Tuhun summoned and interrogated him again, Renwang would not yield. Xiao said with approval, "To serve the people as you do—you will surely rise to high office."

sentences.zh: 以事聞於朝，悉從所請。

translations.literal: He reported the matter to court, and all followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the matter to court, and the petition was fully granted.

sentences.zh: 徙知涿州新城縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Xincheng County in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administer Xincheng County in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 縣與宋接境，驛道所從出。

translations.literal: The county bordered Song territory, and the post road passed through it.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered Song territory and lay on the main post road.

sentences.zh: 人望治不擾，吏民畏愛。

translations.literal: Renwang governed without disturbance; officials and people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang governed without harassment, and officials and commoners alike held him in respect and affection.

sentences.zh: 近臣有聘宋還者，帝問以外事，多薦之，擢中京度支司鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: A court intimate who had been envoy to Song and returned—the emperor asked him about external affairs, and he repeatedly recommended Renwang, who was promoted to Salt and Iron Assessor of the Central Capital Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When a court intimate returned from an embassy to Song, the emperor asked him about affairs abroad, and he repeatedly recommended Renwang, who was promoted to salt and iron assessor of the Central Capital Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 轉南京三司度支判官，公私兼裕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Revenue Assessor of the Southern Capital Three Departments, and both public and private interests were ample.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to revenue assessor of the Southern Capital Three Departments, where both public revenue and private welfare prospered.

sentences.zh: 遷警巡使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Police Patrol Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to police patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 京城獄訟填委，人望處決，無一冤者。

translations.literal: The capital's prisons and lawsuits piled up; Renwang disposed of them, and not one was wrongly convicted.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's courts were buried under pending cases. Renwang disposed of them, and not a single wrongful conviction remained.

sentences.zh: 會檢括戶口，未兩旬而畢。

translations.literal: When a household registration survey was undertaken, it was completed in less than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: When a household registration survey was ordered, he completed it in less than twenty days.

sentences.zh: 同知留守蕭保先怪而問之，人望曰：「民產若括之無遺，他日必長厚斂之弊，大率十得六七足矣。」

translations.literal: Associate Guardian Xiao Baoxian wondered and asked him; Renwang said: "If the people's property is inventoried without omission, later there will surely grow the abuse of heavy exactions—on the whole, obtaining six or seven parts in ten is sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Associate guardian Xiao Baoxian was astonished and asked how he had finished so quickly. Renwang said, "If the people's property is inventoried without omission, officials will surely grow accustomed to heavy exactions. On the whole, recording six or seven parts in ten is sufficient."

sentences.zh: 保先謝曰：「公慮遠，吾不及也。」

translations.literal: Baoxian apologized and said: "Your lordship's foresight is far-reaching—I do not measure up."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxian apologized and said, "Your foresight is far-reaching—I cannot match it."

sentences.zh: 先是，樞密使乙辛竊弄威柄，卒害太子。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Privy Councillor Yixin had usurped authority and in the end harmed the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Privy Councillor Yixin had usurped power and ultimately brought about the crown prince's death.

sentences.zh: 及天祚嗣位，將報父仇，選人望與蕭報恩究其事。

translations.literal: When Tianzuo succeeded to the throne and wished to avenge his father, he selected Renwang and Xiao Bao'en to investigate the matter thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianzuo succeeded and sought to avenge his father, he selected Renwang and Xiao Bao'en to investigate the affair.

sentences.zh: 人望平心以處，所活甚眾。

translations.literal: Renwang handled it with an even heart, and those he spared were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang handled the case impartially, and a great many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 改上京副留守。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Guardian of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice guardian of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 會劇賊趙鐘哥犯闕，劫宮女、禦物，人望率眾捕之。

translations.literal: When the notorious bandit Zhao Zhongge violated the palace precincts, seizing palace women and imperial goods, Renwang led troops to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: When the notorious bandit Zhao Zhongge broke into the palace precincts and seized palace women and imperial goods, Renwang led troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 右臂中矢，炷以艾，力疾馳逐，賊棄所掠而遁。

translations.literal: His right arm was struck by an arrow; he cauterized it with moxa, forced himself despite illness to gallop in pursuit, and the bandits abandoned their plunder and fled.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck his right arm. He cauterized the wound with moxa, forced himself to ride on despite the pain, and the bandits abandoned their loot and fled.

sentences.zh: 人望令關津譏察行旅，悉獲其盜。

translations.literal: Renwang ordered passes and fords to inspect travelers, and all his bandits were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang ordered the frontier passes to inspect travelers, and all the fugitive bandits were captured.

sentences.zh: 尋擢樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Chief Privy Council Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to chief privy council assessor.

sentences.zh: 宰相耶律儼惡人望與己異，遷南京諸宮提轄制置。

translations.literal: The Chief Councillor Yelü Yan hated that Renwang differed from him and transferred him to Commissioner for the Palaces of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Yelü Yan resented Renwang's independence and transferred him to commissioner for the palaces of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 歲中，為保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: Within the year he became Military Commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was appointed military commissioner of Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 有二吏凶暴，民畏如虎。

translations.literal: There were two clerks, fierce and violent; the people feared them as they would tigers.
translations.idiomatic: Two clerks were fierce and violent, and the people feared them as they would tigers.

sentences.zh: 人望假以辭色，陰令發其事，黥配之。

translations.literal: Renwang treated them with mild words and color, secretly ordered their crimes exposed, and had them tattooed and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang treated them with outward courtesy while secretly ordering an investigation; their crimes were exposed and they were tattooed and banished.

sentences.zh: 是歲諸處饑乏，惟人望所治粒食不闕，路不鳴桴。

translations.literal: That year famine afflicted many places; only under Renwang's administration was grain not lacking, and along the roads no alarm drums sounded.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine afflicted many regions, yet only in Renwang's jurisdiction was grain supply uninterrupted, and no alarm drums sounded along the roads.

sentences.zh: 遙授彰義軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was granted in absentia the post of Military Commissioner of Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted in absentia the title of military commissioner of Zhangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 遷中京度支使，始至，府廩皆空；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Revenue Commissioner of the Central Capital; when he first arrived, the government granaries were all empty;
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to revenue commissioner of the Central Capital. When he first arrived, the government granaries were empty;

sentences.zh: 視事半歲，積粟十五萬斛，錢二十萬繦。

translations.literal: after half a year in office he had accumulated a hundred and fifty thousand hu of grain and two hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: yet within half a year in office he had accumulated a hundred and fifty thousand hu of grain and two hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 徙左散騎常侍，累遷樞密直學士。

translations.literal: He was moved to Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and was repeatedly promoted to Academician of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left regular attendant of the cavalry and was promoted in due course to privy council academician.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜參知政事，判南京三司使事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Associate Participant in Governance and concurrently directed the Southern Capital Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed associate participant in governance and concurrently directed the Southern Capital Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 時錢粟出納之弊，惟燕為甚。

translations.literal: At the time abuses in the receipt and disbursement of cash and grain were worst in Yan alone.
translations.idiomatic: At the time abuses in the receipt and disbursement of cash and grain were worst in the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 人望以縑帛為通歷，凡庫物出入，皆使別籍，名曰「臨庫」。

translations.literal: Renwang used silk cloth as a running ledger; all goods entering and leaving the storehouses were made to keep separate registers, called "On-the-Spot Storehouse."
translations.idiomatic: Renwang used silk cloth strips as a running ledger; all goods entering and leaving the storehouses were recorded in separate registers called "On-the-Spot Storehouse."

sentences.zh: 奸人黠吏莫得軒輊，乃以年老揚言道路。

translations.literal: Wicked men and cunning clerks could no longer manipulate affairs, so they spread word along the roads that he was old.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men and cunning clerks could no longer manipulate affairs, so they spread rumors along the roads that he was too old for office.

sentences.zh: 朝論不察，改南院宣徽使，以示優老。

translations.literal: Court opinion did not perceive the truth and changed him to Southern Court Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, to display favor for the aged.
translations.idiomatic: The court failed to see through the scheme and transferred him to southern court commissioner of the palace secretariat as a gesture of honoring his age.

sentences.zh: 逾年，天祚手書「宣馬宣徽」四字詔之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Tianzuo personally wrote the four characters "Summon Ma, Palace Secretariat" in an edict to him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Tianzuo personally wrote the four characters "Summon Ma, Palace Secretariat" in an edict summoning him.

sentences.zh: 既至，諭曰：「以卿為老，誤聽也。」

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor instructed him: "Taking you for old was listening to error."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor said to him, "Believing you too old for office was a mistake on our part."

sentences.zh: 遂拜南院樞密使。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed him Southern Court Privy Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon appointed him southern court privy councillor.

sentences.zh: 人不敢幹以私，用人必公議所當與者。

translations.literal: No one dared to approach him with private requests; in employing men he always chose those whom public deliberation deemed fitting.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared approach him with private requests. In appointments he always chose men whom public deliberation deemed fit.

sentences.zh: 如曹勇義、虞仲文嘗為奸人所擠，人望推薦，皆為名臣。

translations.literal: Such men as Cao Yongyi and Yu Zhongwen had once been squeezed out by villains; Renwang recommended them, and all became famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Cao Yongyi and Yu Zhongwen had once been driven out by schemers; Renwang recommended them, and all rose to become renowned ministers.

sentences.zh: 當時民所甚患者，驛遞、馬牛、旗鼓、鄉正、廳隸、倉司之役，至破產不能給。

translations.literal: What the people then suffered most were corvée duties for post relays, horses and oxen, banners and drums, village heads, hall attendants, and granary offices—so severe that families went bankrupt and still could not meet the demands.
translations.idiomatic: The people's greatest burdens at the time were corvée duties for post relays, horses and oxen, banners and drums, village heads, hall attendants, and granary offices—burdens so heavy that families went bankrupt and still could not meet them.

sentences.zh: 人望使民出錢，官自募役，時以為便。

translations.literal: Renwang had the people pay money while the government hired labor itself; at the time this was considered convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang had the people pay a fee while the government hired labor directly; at the time this was widely regarded as a practical reform.

sentences.zh: 久之請老，以守司徒、兼侍中致仕。

translations.literal: After long service he requested retirement and left office with the titles Guardian Minister of Education and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he requested retirement and left office with the titles guardian minister of education and concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Literary Offering.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Literary Offering.

sentences.zh: 人望有操守，喜怒不形，未嘗附麗求進。

translations.literal: Renwang had integrity in conduct; joy and anger did not show on his face, and he never clung to powerful patrons to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang was a man of integrity; neither joy nor anger showed on his face, and he never curried favor with powerful patrons to advance his career.

sentences.zh: 初除執政，家人賀之。

translations.literal: When he was first appointed to the governing council, his family congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first appointed to the governing council, his family congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 人望愀然曰：「得勿喜，失勿憂。

translations.literal: Renwang said gravely: "In gaining office do not rejoice; in losing it do not grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang said gravely, "When you gain office, do not rejoice; when you lose it, do not grieve.

sentences.zh: 抗之甚高，擠之必酷。」

translations.literal: Raise yourself too high, and when you are pushed down the fall will surely be cruel."
translations.idiomatic: Raise yourself too high, and when you are pushed down the fall will be cruel."

sentences.zh: 其畏慎如此。

translations.literal: Such was his caution and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his caution and restraint.

sentences.zh: 耶律鐸魯斡，字乙辛隱，季父房之後。

translations.literal: Yelü Duoluwo, styled Yixin Yin, was a descendant of the Younger Father's House.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Duoluwo, styled Yixin Yin, was a descendant of the Younger Father's House.

sentences.zh: 廉約重義。

translations.literal: He was frugal and abstemious, and valued righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was frugal and abstemious and valued righteousness.

sentences.zh: 重熙末，給事誥院。

translations.literal: Late in Chongxi he served in the Edict Office.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Chongxi era he served in the Edict Office.

sentences.zh: 咸雍中，累遷同知南京留守事。

translations.literal: During Xianyong he was repeatedly promoted to Associate Administrator of the Southern Capital Guardian's Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianyong era he was promoted in due course to associate administrator of the Southern Capital guardian's office.

sentences.zh: 被召，以部民懇留，乃賜詔褒獎。

translations.literal: When summoned to court, because the people of his district earnestly begged him to remain, an edict was bestowed commending and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to court, the people of his district earnestly begged him to remain, and the throne issued an edict commending and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 大康初，改西南面招討使，為北面林牙，遷左夷離畢。

translations.literal: Early in Dakang he was changed to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit, became Northern Court Forest Ya, and was promoted to Left Yilübi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dakang era he was appointed pacification commissioner of the southwestern circuit, then northern court forest ya, and was promoted to left yilübi.

sentences.zh: 大安五年，拜南府宰相。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Da'an he was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Da'an era he was appointed chancellor of the southern office.

sentences.zh: 壽隆初，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Early in Shoulong he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shoulong era he retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 鐸魯斡所至有聲，吏民畏愛。

translations.literal: Wherever Duoluwo went he won renown; officials and people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Duoluwo served he won renown, and officials and commoners alike held him in respect and affection.

sentences.zh: 及退居鄉里，子普古為烏古部節度使，遣人來迎。

translations.literal: When he retired to his home district, his son Pugu was Military Commissioner of the Wugu Circuit and sent men to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When he retired to his home district, his son Pugu, then military commissioner of the Wugu circuit, sent men to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 既至，見積委甚富。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he saw accumulated stores very rich.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he found the stores piled with great wealth.

sentences.zh: 謂普古曰：「辭親入仕，當以裕國安民為事。

translations.literal: He said to Pugu: "Leaving kin to enter office, one ought to make enriching the state and settling the people one's task.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Pugu, "When one leaves one's kin to enter office, enriching the state and settling the people ought to be one's task.

sentences.zh: 枉道欺君，以茍貨利，非吾誌也。」

translations.literal: To bend the Way and deceive the ruler, to seek base profit—this is not my aim."
translations.idiomatic: To bend principle and deceive the ruler for base profit—that is not my aim."

sentences.zh: 命駕而歸。

translations.literal: He ordered his carriage and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his carriage and returned home.

sentences.zh: 普古後為盜所殺。

translations.literal: Pugu was later killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu was later killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 楊遵勖，字益誡，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Zunxu, styled Yijie, was a man of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunxu, styled Yijie, was a native of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 重熙十九年登進士第，調儒州軍事判官，累遷樞密院副承旨。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Chongxi he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Military Assessor of Ruzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to Deputy Assessor of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Chongxi era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed military assessor of Ruzhou, and was promoted in due course to deputy assessor of the privy council.

sentences.zh: 咸雍三年，為宋國賀正使；

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianyong he was envoy to Song to offer New Year's congratulations;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xianyong era he served as envoy to Song to offer New Year's congratulations;

sentences.zh: 還，遷都承旨。

translations.literal: on his return he was promoted to Chief Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: on his return he was promoted to chief assessor.

sentences.zh: 天下之事，叢於樞府，簿書填委。

translations.literal: Affairs of the realm clustered in the Privy Council, and documents piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of the realm were concentrated in the privy council, and documents piled up without end.

sentences.zh: 遵勖一目五行俱下，剖決如流，敷奏詳敏。

translations.literal: Zunxu read five lines at a glance, decided cases like flowing water, and presented memorials in detail and with quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: Zunxu read five lines at a glance, disposed of cases with flowing efficiency, and presented memorials with precision and quick wit.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 奉詔征戶部逋錢，得四十餘萬緡，拜樞密直學士，改樞密副使。

translations.literal: By imperial order he collected overdue revenue funds and obtained more than four hundred thousand strings; he was appointed Academician of the Privy Council and changed to Vice Privy Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he collected overdue revenue funds and recovered more than four hundred thousand strings of cash. He was appointed privy council academician and then vice privy councillor.

sentences.zh: 大康初，參知政事，徙知樞密院事，兼門下侍郎、平章事，拜南府宰相。

translations.literal: Early in Dakang he became Associate Participant in Governance, was moved to Administrator of the Privy Council, concurrently Gate Attendant and Grand Councillor, and was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dakang era he became associate participant in governance, was appointed administrator of the privy council, and concurrently gate attendant and grand councillor, then chancellor of the southern office.

sentences.zh: 耶律乙辛誣皇太子，詔遵勖與燕哥按其事，遵勖不敢正言，時議短之。

translations.literal: Yelü Yixin slandered the Crown Prince; an edict ordered Zunxu and Yange to investigate the matter. Zunxu did not dare speak straight, and opinion at the time faulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yixin framed the crown prince, and an edict ordered Zunxu and Yange to investigate. Zunxu did not dare speak plainly, and contemporary opinion faulted him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋拜北府宰相。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Chancellor of the Northern Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was appointed chancellor of the northern office.

sentences.zh: 大安中暴卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In Da'an he died suddenly, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly during the Da'an era, at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈守司空，謚康懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Guardian Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Kangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted guardian minister of works and given the posthumous title Kangyi.

sentences.zh: 子晦，終昭文館直學士。

translations.literal: His son Hui ended his career as Academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui ended his career as academician of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 王棠，涿州新城人。

translations.literal: Wang Tang was a man of Xincheng in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tang was a native of Xincheng in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 博古善屬文。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned in antiquity and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned in antiquity and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 重熙十五年擢進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chongxi he was selected as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Chongxi era he was selected as jinshi.

sentences.zh: 鄉貢、禮部、廷試對皆第一。

translations.literal: In the provincial presentation, the Ministry of Rites, and the palace examination responses he ranked first in all.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the provincial presentation, the Ministry of Rites examination, and the palace examination responses.

sentences.zh: 累遷上京鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in due course to salt and iron commissioner of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 或誣以賄，無狀，釋之。

translations.literal: Someone slandered him with bribery, but there was no substance; he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused him of bribery, but the charge had no substance and he was released.

sentences.zh: 遷東京戶部使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of the Eastern Capital Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大康二年，遼東饑，民多死，請賑恤，從之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dakang eastern Liao suffered famine; many among the people died. He requested relief and succor, and the court assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dakang era eastern Liao suffered famine and many people died. He petitioned for relief and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為樞密副使，拜南府宰相。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered court as Vice Privy Councillor and was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered court as vice privy councillor and was appointed chancellor of the southern office.

sentences.zh: 大安末，卒。

translations.literal: Late in Da'an he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died late in the Da'an era.

sentences.zh: 棠練達朝政，臨事不怠，在政府修明法度，有聲。

translations.literal: Tang was practiced in court affairs, never slack in handling business, and in government refined and clarified the laws—he had renown.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was thoroughly versed in court affairs and never slack in handling business. In government he refined and clarified the laws and won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 論曰：孟子謂「民為貴，社稷次之」，司牧者當如何以盡心。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Mencius said "the people are precious, the altars of soil and grain come next"—how ought those who tend the flock give their utmost hearts?
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Mencius declared that "the people are precious, the altars of soil and grain come next"—how ought those who govern the people give their utmost devotion?

sentences.zh: 公鼎奏罷完堤役以息民，拒公主假貸以守法，單騎行郡，化盜為良，庶幾召、杜之美。

translations.literal: Gongding memorialized to halt dike labor and give the people rest, refused the princess's loans to uphold the law, rode alone through the commandery and transformed bandits into good men—perhaps approaching the beauty of Zhao and Du.
translations.idiomatic: Gongding memorialized to halt dike corvée and give the people rest, refused the princess's loans to uphold the law, rode alone through the commandery and transformed bandits into loyal subjects—approaching, one might say, the renown of Zhao Ji and Du Shi.

sentences.zh: 文知易州，雨暍應禱，蝗不為災。

translations.literal: Wen governed Yizhou; drought and heat responded to his prayers with rain, and locusts did not become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Wen governed Yizhou: drought responded to his prayers with rain, and locusts did not become a calamity.

sentences.zh: 人望為民不避囚系，判度支，公私兼裕，亦卓乎未易及已。

translations.literal: Renwang for the people's sake did not shrink from imprisonment, judged revenue affairs, and made both public and private interests ample—also outstanding and not easy to match.
translations.idiomatic: Renwang for the people's sake did not shrink from imprisonment, directed revenue affairs with both public and private interests prospering—also outstanding and not easily matched.

sentences.zh: 鐸魯斡吏畏民愛，楊遵勖決事如流，真能吏哉！

translations.literal: Duoluwo: officials feared him and the people loved him; Yang Zunxu decided affairs like flowing water—truly capable officials!
translations.idiomatic: Duoluwo was feared by officials and loved by the people; Yang Zunxu disposed of affairs with flowing efficiency—truly capable administrators indeed!
